rules.title: California Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of paid leave at the start or end of the shift to vote when the employee lacks sufficient time outside working hours; the employee gives at least 2 working days notice

citations.source: Cal. Elec. Code §§14000-14003 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California — Victim Leave for Court and Safety (all employers)

params.covered_reasons: judicial proceedings related to the crime; relief such as restraining orders for the safety of the employee or a child

result.summary: All employers: no discharge or retaliation for time off to appear in court as a crime victim or to seek a restraining order or other relief for safety (Lab. Code 230(c), (e)); reasonable safety accommodations required on request (230(f)). Employee may use accrued paid leave. Expanded 2025 (AB 2499) to victims of 'qualifying acts of violence' and moved to Gov. Code 12945.8 for CRD enforcement.

rules.title: California — Victim Leave for Medical, Counseling and Relocation (25+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, victim services, counseling, safety planning, relocation

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must also allow unpaid time off for medical attention, victim services, psychological counseling, safety planning and relocation (Lab. Code 230.1); from 2025 the right is in Gov. Code 12945.8 and family members of victims are covered for certain purposes.

rules.title: USERRA — Uniformed Services Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: uniformed services (active duty, reserve and National Guard federal duty, training)

result.summary: All employers must grant unpaid leave for service in the uniformed services and reemploy the employee in the escalator position after up to 5 cumulative years of service, with no discrimination or retaliation; health coverage continues up to 24 months at the employee's expense. State-ordered National Guard duty is covered only by state law.

rules.title: California — State Military Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: state active duty and National Guard or state militia service

result.summary: No discrimination for state or federal military membership or service (§394); up to 17 days a year of unpaid leave for reserve, Guard or Naval Militia training (§395.06); Guard members on state active duty must be reinstated and may not be discharged without cause for one year (§395.05, §394.5). (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Workplace Fairness, State Laws on Military Leave (50-state survey, used for encoding)
Paycor, Military Leave Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California — Civil Air Patrol Leave (10 days, 16+ employees)

params.service_type: Civil Air Patrol emergency service operations or training

result.summary: Employers with 16 or more employees must give Civil Air Patrol volunteers up to 10 days a year of unpaid leave for emergency service operations (3 days per mission), with reinstatement and no loss of benefits.

citations.source: Paycor, Military Leave Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California — Military Spouse Leave (10 days, 25+ employees)

params.trigger: service member on leave from deployment during a period of military conflict

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must give an employee who works 20 or more hours a week up to 10 days of unpaid leave while their spouse or domestic partner is on leave from deployment during a military conflict; 2 business days' notice.

rules.title: California Family & Medical Leave (12 weeks, paid)

result.summary: 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave

citations.source: California Family Rights Act (CFRA) + CA PFL

rules.title: Federal FMLA — Employee Eligibility

result.summary: Employee is FMLA-eligible: entitled to up to 12 weeks unpaid job-protected leave

citations.source: Family and Medical Leave Act, 29 U.S.C. §2612

rules.title: California — Accrued Vacation at Separation (payout required)

result.summary: Vested vacation and PTO are wages: all accrued, unused time must be paid at the final rate on separation and use-it-or-lose-it policies are void (reasonable accrual caps allowed); a CBA may provide otherwise. (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Paycor, PTO Payout Laws by State (survey used for encoding)
Patriot Software, PTO Payout Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California — Bereavement Leave (5 days, 5+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, parent-in-law, sibling, grandparent, grandchild

result.summary: Employers with 5 or more employees must give an employee with 30 days of service up to 5 days of bereavement leave per death of a covered family member, taken within 3 months; unpaid unless the employer's policy pays, and the employee may use accrued paid leave. Reproductive loss leave (5 days) added 2024 (Gov. Code 12945.6).

rules.title: California Paid Sick Leave (1 hr per 30 hrs worked, up to 40 hrs/yr)

result.summary: 40 hours of paid sick leave per year, accrued at 1 hour per 30 hours worked

rules.title: Los Angeles Paid Sick Leave (1 hr per 30 hrs worked, up to 48 hrs)

result.summary: 48 hours of paid sick leave per year, accrued at 1 hour per 30 hours worked

citations.source: Los Angeles Paid Sick Leave Ordinance

rules.title: California — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th day of employment; the employer may set a minimum increment of up to 2 hours and may cap use at 40 hours or 5 days a year (SB 616, 2024).

rules.title: California — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Accrued leave carries over; the total balance may be capped at 80 hours or 10 days. Frontloading 40 hours/5 days at the start of each year removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within one year.

result.summary: Scheduling a 16-17 year old to work past 10:00 PM on a school night in CA

rules.title: California Minimum Wage

result.summary: $16.50 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Federal Minimum Wage (FLSA)

result.summary: $7.25 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Los Angeles Minimum Wage

result.summary: $18.42 per hour minimum wage

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code §187.00 et seq.

rules.title: California Daily Overtime (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 8 in a day

rules.title: California Double Time (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: 2x regular rate for hours over 12 in a day

rules.title: Federal Weekly Overtime (FLSA)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a week

rules.title: Federal Workweek Definition (FLSA)

result.summary: Overtime is computed over a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that may begin on any day and hour; it may be changed only permanently and not to evade overtime, and hours may not be averaged across weeks

rules.title: California Workday and Workweek Definition

result.summary: Daily overtime is measured over a fixed 24-hour workday and weekly and seventh-day overtime over a fixed 168-hour workweek, each starting at a time the employer sets and changes only for legitimate business reasons

rules.title: California Seventh Consecutive Day: 1.5x for the First 8 Hours (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: The first 8 hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek are paid at 1.5x the regular rate (AB 60, effective 2000-01-01). Does not apply to employees on a valid alternative workweek schedule.

rules.title: California Seventh Consecutive Day: 2x After 8 Hours (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: Hours over 8 on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek are paid at 2x the regular rate.

rules.title: Federal — EAP Exemption Salary Level $684/week (29 CFR 541.600)

result.summary: An executive, administrative or professional employee is exempt from FLSA overtime only if paid on a salary basis at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year), plus $107,432 total annual compensation for the highly compensated employee test. The 2024 rule raising these levels was vacated (E.D. Tex. 2024-11-15) and formally rescinded by DOL on 2026-05-15, so the 2019 levels remain in force. States may set higher thresholds.

rules.title: California — Exempt Salary Threshold $1,352/week (2x Minimum Wage), 2026

params.basis: 2 x state minimum wage ($16.90) x 40 hours; indexed annually

result.summary: Executive, administrative and professional employees are exempt only if paid a monthly salary of at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time employment (Labor Code §515(a)): $1,352 a week / $5,858.67 a month / $70,304 a year at the 2026 minimum wage of $16.90. Health care and large fast-food employers covered by industry minimum wages use twice that wage ($1,600 a week at $20). Rises each January with the minimum wage.

rules.title: California Reporting Time Pay (half scheduled shift, min 2 hrs, max 4 hrs)

result.summary: Half the scheduled shift hours at regular rate (minimum 2 hours, maximum 4 hours)

rules.title: California Second Reporting Time Pay (minimum 2 hours)

result.summary: Pay for minimum 2 hours at regular rate for second reporting in one workday

rules.title: California Split Shift Premium (+1 hr at state minimum wage)

result.summary: 1 additional hour at the state minimum wage rate (unless total daily earnings already exceed min wage × (hours worked + 1))

rules.title: California — Pay Frequency

params.notes: Weekly or biweekly schedules must pay within 7 days of the period end; executive, administrative and professional employees may be paid monthly by the 26th

result.summary: Wages must be paid at least twice a month on regular paydays designated in advance; work in the 1st-15th is paid by the 26th and the 16th-end by the 10th.

rules.title: FLSA — Wage Deductions

result.summary: Under the FLSA, deductions for items that primarily benefit the employer (uniforms, tools, cash shortages, damage) may not reduce pay below the minimum wage or cut into overtime.

citations.source: 29 CFR §531.35 (wages must be paid free and clear)
US DOL Fact Sheet #16: Deductions from Wages for Uniforms and Other Facilities

rules.title: California — Wage Deductions

params.penalty: civil penalties under §225.5 plus waiting-time and PAGA exposure

result.summary: Employers may not take back any part of wages; only deductions required by law or expressly authorized in writing for the employee's benefit are allowed, and shortages, breakage or damage may not be deducted absent dishonesty, willfulness or gross negligence.

citations.source: Ezel, Employee Wage Deduction Requirements by State (survey)

rules.title: Equal Pay Act of 1963 — Equal Pay

params.notes: Covers all FLSA-covered employers; NLRA §7 separately protects most non-supervisory employees who discuss wages

result.summary: Employees of the opposite sex doing equal work (equal skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) in the same establishment must be paid equally unless a seniority, merit, production or other factor-other-than-sex system explains the gap.

rules.title: California — Equal Pay

params.notes: Race and ethnicity added 2017-01-01; prior salary may not justify a gap

result.summary: Employees of another sex, race or ethnicity doing substantially similar work (viewed as a composite of skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) must be paid equally unless the whole gap is explained by seniority, merit, production or a bona fide factor other than the protected trait; employees may discuss and disclose wages.

citations.source: Paycor, Pay Equity and State-by-State Laws (survey)

rules.title: California First Meal Break (>5 hours)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 5+ hours

rules.title: California — Meal Break Required (shifts > 5 hrs)

result.summary: California requires a 30-minute meal break for shifts over 5 hours. Ensure a break is scheduled.

rules.title: California Second Meal Break (>10 hours)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 10+ hours

rules.title: California — First Meal Period May Be Waived on Shifts of 6 Hours or Less

result.summary: When the total work period is no more than 6 hours the first meal period may be waived by mutual consent of employer and employee (Labor Code §512(a)). The consent need not be written but should be documented; the employee may withdraw it.

rules.title: California — First Meal Period Cannot Be Waived on Shifts Over 6 Hours (On-Duty Meal Only by Written Agreement)

result.summary: A first meal period on a shift longer than 6 hours cannot be waived. A paid on-duty meal period is permitted only when the nature of the work prevents relief from all duty and the parties have a written agreement that the employee may revoke at any time (Wage Orders §11). Otherwise a missed or late meal period owes one hour of premium pay (§226.7).

rules.title: California — Second Meal Period May Be Waived on Shifts of 10 to 12 Hours

result.summary: When the total work period is more than 10 but no more than 12 hours the second meal period may be waived by mutual consent, but only if the first meal period was not waived (Labor Code §512(a)). On shifts over 12 hours the second meal period cannot be waived outside the health care exception.

rules.title: Los Angeles — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or contractors, the employer must offer the work in writing to current employees for 72 hours (or until accepted) when they are qualified

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (offer of additional work) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — 14-Day Advance Notice Required (Retail)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each change the employer makes to a posted schedule with less than 14 days notice that adds time or changes the date, time or location with no loss of hours

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.00 et seq. (Fair Work Week Ordinance)
citations.section: LAMC Art. 5 (advance notice and predictability pay)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <14 days notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each hour not worked when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer reduces a shift by at least 15 minutes or cancels it

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: Before hire, and within 10 days of a request, the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's work schedule

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (good faith estimate) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours, shifts or changes not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice; the employee's consent to a change must be in writing

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (right to decline) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Fair Work Week: Right to Request Hours, Times and Locations; Written Reason for Denial

result.summary: A covered retail employee may request a preference for certain hours, times or locations of work. The employer may accept or decline, but a denial must state the reason in writing. Employee-requested changes do not trigger predictability pay.

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.03 (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: California Lactation Accommodation

result.summary: Reasonable break time to express milk, running with paid rest breaks where possible and otherwise unpaid; a private non-bathroom space is required (space-only hardship exemption under 50 employees)

citations.source: Cal. Labor Code §§1030-1034 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California Rest Break (10 min per 4 hours worked)

result.summary: 10-minute rest break for shifts of 3.5+ hours

rules.title: California — Rest Break Required (per 4 hrs worked)

result.summary: California requires a paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked. Ensure rest breaks are scheduled.

rules.title: Federal Lactation Break Time (PUMP Act)

result.summary: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk for one year after the child's birth, in a private non-bathroom space; unpaid unless the employee is not fully relieved or uses a paid break (employers under 50 may claim undue hardship)

citations.source: Fair Labor Standards Act §18d (PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act)

rules.title: California Day of Rest (1 day off per 7-day workweek)

result.summary: Scheduling an employee to work more than 6 consecutive days without a day of rest. Employee may voluntarily choose to work the 7th day. Exemptions for emergencies and certain industries.

rules.title: Los Angeles — 10-Hour Rest Period (Retail)

result.summary: 1.5x pay rate for hours worked within the 10-hour rest period

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.00 et seq. (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: California — Final Wages on Discharge

params.penalty: waiting time penalty of one day's wages per day late, up to 30 days (§203)

result.summary: All wages are due immediately on discharge or layoff; late payment accrues a waiting time penalty of a day's pay per day up to 30 days.

rules.title: California — Final Wages on Resignation

params.notice_shortens_deadline: due on the last day if the employee gave at least 72 hours' notice
params.penalty: waiting time penalty of one day's wages per day late, up to 30 days (§203)

result.summary: Employees who quit without 72 hours' notice are paid within 72 hours; with 72 hours' notice, on the last day.

rules.title: California Mini-WARN Act (60-day notice, 75+ employees)

result.summary: California requires 60 days advance written notice before plant closing or mass layoff affecting 75+ employees.

params.name: minimum_minutes

params.name: nonworking_hours_exception
params.description: No leave is owed when the employee has at least this many consecutive non-working hours while polls are open

params.name: employer_sets_time
params.description: Whether the employer may designate when the leave is taken

obligations.name: Minor work-hour curfew
obligations.description: Earliest start or latest end time a minor may work, often differing on school nights.

params.name: age_min
params.description: Youngest age covered

params.name: age_max
params.description: Oldest age covered

params.name: latest_end_hour
params.description: Work must end by this hour (21 = 9 PM; 24 and above means after midnight)

params.name: earliest_start_hour
params.description: Work may not start before this hour

params.name: school_night
params.description: True when the limit applies only before a school day, false when it applies only outside the school year; omitted when it applies always

obligations.name: Minor daily hours limit
obligations.description: Most hours a minor may work in one day.

params.name: age_min
params.description: Youngest age covered

params.name: age_max
params.description: Oldest age covered

params.name: max_hours
params.description: Maximum hours in the day

params.name: school_day
params.description: True for school days, false for non-school days; omitted when it applies always

obligations.name: Minor weekly hours limit
obligations.description: Most hours a minor may work in one week.

params.name: age_min
params.description: Youngest age covered

params.name: age_max
params.description: Oldest age covered

params.name: max_hours
params.description: Maximum hours in the week

params.name: school_week
params.description: True for weeks when school is in session, false for non-school weeks; omitted when it applies always

obligations.name: Equal pay
obligations.description: Employees doing the same or comparable work may not be paid differently because of a protected characteristic; some states also protect employees who discuss wages.

params.name: comparison_standard
params.description: How alike two jobs must be for a pay difference to need a lawful justification; discrimination_statute_only means pay bias is reached only through the general anti-discrimination law

params.name: protected_classes
params.description: Characteristics the pay comparison protects

params.name: min_employees
params.description: Employer size at which the law attaches

params.name: pay_secrecy_prohibited
params.description: Whether the state bars employers from forbidding or punishing wage discussions

params.name: notes
params.description: Lawful justifications, remedies and recent amendments

obligations.name: Exempt salary threshold
obligations.description: The lowest weekly salary at which an executive, administrative or professional employee may be treated as exempt from overtime; below it the employee is owed overtime regardless of duties.

params.name: weekly_salary
params.description: Minimum weekly salary for the exemption

params.name: annual_salary
params.description: The same threshold expressed per year

params.name: basis
params.description: How the figure is set (fixed, multiple of the minimum wage, indexed)

obligations.name: Pay frequency
obligations.description: How often wages must be paid and how soon after the pay period ends; many states let exempt or salaried staff be paid less often.

params.name: minimum_frequency
params.description: Least frequent lawful pay schedule for the employees the rule covers; none means the state sets no frequency

params.name: max_days_between_paydays
params.description: Longest lawful gap between paydays where the statute counts days

params.name: max_lag_days
params.description: Days after the end of a pay period by which wages for that period must be paid

params.name: lag_business_days
params.description: Whether max_lag_days counts business days only

params.name: exempt_may_be_monthly
params.description: Whether exempt, executive, administrative or professional employees may be paid monthly

params.name: applies_to
params.description: Who the frequency rule covers when narrower than all employees

params.name: notes
params.description: Waivers, agency approvals and other wrinkles

obligations.name: Wage deductions
obligations.description: What an employer may take out of a paycheck beyond taxes and court orders, whether the employee must authorize it in writing, and whether cash shortages, breakage or damage may ever be charged back.

params.name: written_authorization_required
params.description: What the employee must sign (or be told) before a voluntary deduction; not_required means the state has no general consent statute and only the FLSA floor applies

params.name: shortage_damage_deductions
params.description: Whether cash shortages, breakage, lost or damaged property may be deducted and on what condition

params.name: below_minimum_wage_prohibited
params.description: Whether employer-benefit deductions may never reduce pay below the minimum wage

params.name: penalty
params.description: Statutory remedy for an unlawful deduction

params.name: notes
params.description: Caps, timing, revocation and other wrinkles

obligations.name: Workweek and workday definition
obligations.description: The fixed, regularly recurring period over which overtime hours are counted; it may start on any day and hour but cannot be moved to avoid overtime.

params.name: period_hours
params.description: Length of the workweek in hours (168 = seven consecutive 24-hour periods)

params.name: workday_hours
params.description: Length of the workday where daily overtime applies (24 consecutive hours)

params.name: fixed_recurring
params.description: The period must be fixed and regularly recurring; changes are allowed only if permanent and not designed to evade overtime

obligations.name: Overtime premium
obligations.description: A multiple of the regular rate owed for hours past a daily or weekly threshold.

params.name: multiplier
params.description: Multiple of the regular rate (1.5, 2)

params.name: threshold_hours
params.description: Hours after which the premium applies

params.name: period
params.description: Whether the threshold is per workday, per workweek, or applies to hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of the workweek

obligations.name: Reporting time pay
obligations.description: Minimum pay owed when an employee reports for a scheduled shift and is sent home early or not put to work.

params.name: minimum_hours
params.description: Minimum hours that must be paid

params.name: maximum_hours
params.description: Cap on the hours owed under the rule

params.name: fraction_of_scheduled
params.description: Fraction of the scheduled shift that must be paid (0.5 = half)

params.name: rate_basis
params.description: Which rate the hours are paid at

obligations.name: Schedule change premium
obligations.description: Predictability pay owed when the employer changes a posted schedule inside the notice window.

params.name: amount
params.description: Premium amount, in the unit given

params.name: unit
params.description: How the amount is expressed: hours of pay per affected shift, a flat dollar amount, or a percent of the subtracted hours

params.name: notice_window_days
params.description: Changes made with less than this much notice trigger the premium

params.name: change_type
params.description: Which schedule changes trigger the premium: hours added (incl. added shifts), hours reduced (incl. cancellations and early send-home), a time or location change with no change in hours, an on-call shift the employee was not called in for, or any change

obligations.name: Split shift premium
obligations.description: Extra pay owed when the workday is split by an unpaid, non-meal gap.

params.name: amount
params.description: Hours of pay owed

params.name: rate_basis
params.description: Which rate the premium is paid at

obligations.name: Weekly day of rest
obligations.description: The employee must get a day (24 consecutive hours) of rest in each week or run of consecutive days.

params.name: max_consecutive_days
params.description: Most consecutive days the employee may be scheduled

params.name: rest_hours
params.description: Consecutive hours of rest owed in each period

params.name: period_days
params.description: Length of the period the rest is owed in (usually 7)

obligations.name: Offer of hours to existing employees
obligations.description: Before hiring new staff or using a staffing agency to cover hours, the employer must offer those hours to existing (part-time) employees.

params.name: offer_window_hours
params.description: How long the offer must stay open to existing employees before the employer may hire (72 hours = 3 days)

params.name: max_part_time_hours
params.description: Weekly hours below which an employee counts as part-time for the offer, where the law sets one

synonyms: offer of work to existing employees

obligations.name: Rest between shifts (clopening)
obligations.description: A closing shift followed by an opening shift with less than the required rest is barred, or owes a premium, unless the employee consents.

params.name: rest_hours
params.description: Minimum hours between the end of one shift and the start of the next

params.name: amount
params.description: Premium amount, in the unit given

params.name: unit
params.description: How the premium is expressed

obligations.name: Good faith estimate of hours
obligations.description: At hire (and on request or when circumstances change) the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's expected hours, days and shifts.

params.name: lookback_days
params.description: Period the estimate is based on or must be revisited over, where the law sets one (Philadelphia and Chicago: 90 days)

obligations.name: Right to decline late-added hours
obligations.description: The employee may refuse hours or shifts the employer adds or moves inside the notice window; working them needs the employee's consent.

params.name: notice_days
params.description: Hours added with less than this much notice may be declined

obligations.name: Right to request schedule changes
obligations.description: The employee may ask for changes to hours, days, times, location or a flexible or predictable arrangement without retaliation; some laws also oblige the employer to consider, answer in writing, or grant the request absent a business reason.

params.name: must_grant_unless_business_reason
params.description: Whether the employer must grant the request unless it has a bona fide business reason or undue hardship (false = consider or respond only)

params.name: written_response_days
params.description: Days the employer has to answer in writing

params.name: requests_per_year
params.description: Requests the employer must entertain per year

params.name: retaliation_only
params.description: True when the law only bars retaliation for asking

obligations.name: Final paycheck deadline
obligations.description: When all wages earned through separation must be paid, which usually differs for a discharge and a resignation.

params.name: deadline
params.description: Shape of the deadline; no_state_law means only the FLSA next-regular-payday practice applies

params.name: hours
params.description: Hours after separation (or after demand) when deadline is within_hours

params.name: days
params.description: Days after separation when the deadline counts days

params.name: business_days
params.description: Whether the day count excludes weekends and holidays

params.name: runs_from_demand
params.description: Whether the clock starts at the employee's demand for payment rather than at separation

params.name: notice_shortens_deadline
params.description: How advance notice from the employee changes the deadline

params.name: penalty
params.description: Statutory penalty for late payment

obligations.name: Mass layoff / plant closing notice (WARN)
obligations.description: Advance written notice owed to employees and the state before a plant closing or mass layoff.

params.name: notice_days
params.description: Days of advance notice required

params.name: employee_threshold
params.description: Employer size (or affected count) at which the law applies

obligations.name: Minimum wage
obligations.description: The lowest hourly rate an employer may pay a covered employee.

params.name: rate
params.description: Minimum hourly rate
